title: split-provisioning-adapters-and-introduce-staged-recovery-plan
creator: Sofia Ramos
description: Background: The capacity planner and node lifecycle codebase has accreted multiple provisioning paths for ephemeral, reserved and burst nodes. This tight coupling increases blast radius for changes, slows down autoscaler improvements, and makes a fast "recovery" path for transient node loss difficult to reason about. Goal: decouple provisioning adapters from planner core, extract lifecycle behaviors into swappable plugins, and implement a staged fast-recovery flow that can reclaim or replace nodes with minimal reconciliation work. Outcomes: 1) Smaller, testable adapter interfaces; 2) Fast-path for node replacement that avoids full snapshot merges for common cases; 3) Reduced tail latencies during bulk node churn; 4) Clear migration path for LegacyLeasePool users. Scope: - Define a minimal ProvisioningAdapter interface (Create/MarkStaged/Finalize/Abort/Status) and replace the 3 ad-hoc provisioning implementations with adapters. - Factor out node lifecycle state transitions into LifecyclePlugin implementations (GracefulDrain, Fencing, Quarantine, FastReplace). - Implement staged recovery: quick-allocate -> attach-lease -> health-probe -> finalize, with a 90s optimistic window to avoid heavy planner snapshot operations. - Add feature flag gated rollout with rollout phases per pool (canary 1 pool, 10% pools, full). - Maintain backward compatibility via a LegacyAdapter that translates existing flows onto the new interface. Non-goals: full rewrite of capacity snapshot merge logic (leave for follow-up), changing autoscaler policy language. Acceptance criteria: - Unit tests cover each adapter and lifecycle plugin (>= 80% coverage for new modules). - End-to-end integration test that simulates 500 node churn with less than 10% increase in average allocation latency vs baseline, and < 2x tail latency reduction on 99th percentile. - Feature flag enables canary rollout; metrics emitted for success/failure rate, time-to-finalize, and planner snapshot avoidance counts. - Migration guide and one migration script for LegacyLeasePool -> LegacyAdapter. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: subtle state races during optimistic finalize. Mitigation: add a short coordinator lock per node ID and conservative fallback to planner snapshot. - Risk: increased complexity in adapters. Mitigation: keep interfaces small and put heavy logic in tests and examples. Rollout plan: - Week 1: Interface design and unit prototypes (canary flag). - Week 2: Implement LegacyAdapter and one new adapter for ephemeral nodes. - Week 3: Integration test harness and simulated churn benchmark. - Week 4: Canary rollout to a single pool, monitor metrics, iterate. Monitoring and SLOs: - Dashboards: "adapter_success_rate", "fast_recovery_finalization_time_ms", "planner_snapshot_invocations_avoided". - Alert: adapter_error_rate > 1% sustained for 5m. Documentation: add design doc and migration guide linked below.
